lessons.subject: Basic Science
lessons.title: Keeping Our Water Safe
lessons.objective: Identify ways to keep drinking water safe and explain why cleanliness matters.

sections.heading: Why clean water matters
sections.text: Water is important for drinking, cooking and washing. Water that looks clear may still contain germs. Germs can make people sick.

sections.heading: Safe water habits
sections.text: Use water from a safe source. Where needed, a responsible adult can boil water and allow it to cool in a clean, covered container. Never handle boiling water without adult help. Keep cups and water containers clean.

sections.heading: Try it
sections.text: Draw two water containers: one open and one covered. Explain which is safer for storing drinking water and why.

questions.prompt: Which container helps protect stored drinking water?
questions.explanation: A clean cover helps prevent dirt and insects from entering stored water.

questions.prompt: Can clear-looking water still contain germs?
questions.explanation: Some germs cannot be seen with the eyes.
Boiling water can cause serious burns.

lessons.subject: Civic Education
lessons.title: Helping Our Community
lessons.objective: Describe responsible actions that make a community safer and kinder.

sections.heading: What is a community?
sections.text: A community is a group of people who live, learn or work together. A school, street and village can each be a community.

sections.heading: Responsibility in action
sections.text: We can help by putting waste in bins, caring for shared spaces, listening respectfully and reporting unsafe situations to a trusted adult.

sections.heading: Try it
sections.text: Write one problem in your school and two respectful ways classmates can work together to improve it.

questions.prompt: Which action helps a shared school space?
questions.explanation: Proper waste disposal helps keep shared spaces clean.

questions.prompt: Who should a child tell about an unsafe situation?
questions.explanation: A trusted adult can help respond safely.

choices: People who live, learn or work together
questions.explanation: Communities are groups of people connected by place or activity.

lessons.subject: Agricultural Science
lessons.title: Soil and Plant Growth
lessons.objective: Identify three basic soil types and explain how soil supports plants.

sections.heading: Why soil matters
sections.text: Soil supports plant roots and provides water and nutrients. Farmers study soil to understand which crops may grow well.

sections.heading: Three common soil types
sections.text: Sandy soil has relatively large particles and drains quickly. Clay soil has fine particles and often holds more water. Loamy soil is a mixture that can support many crops when managed well.

sections.heading: Try it
sections.text: With a teacher, compare dry samples of sandy and clay soil. Describe the texture and discuss why different crops may need different soil conditions.

questions.prompt: Which soil usually drains water quickly?
questions.explanation: Larger sand particles leave spaces that let water drain more easily.

questions.prompt: What do roots gain from soil?
questions.explanation: Roots absorb water and mineral nutrients.

questions.prompt: Which soil is often a mixture of sand, silt and clay?
questions.explanation: Loam is a mixture of soil particle sizes.
